alternatives.argument: The local Definition explicitly gives the C2 neighborhood extension, orientation-preserving diffeomorphism, positive Jacobian, physical mesh velocity, and finite transported boundary presentation. It imports no thesis result; the Jacobi and Reynolds identities are proved in their own carriers.

The complete alternative proof is local: step 1.1 expands det(F+hH+o(h)) by permutations to obtain J tr(F^{-1}H); step 2.1 differentiates w_m(A_t(xi),t)=partial_t A_t(xi), applies the chain rule, and uses trace invariance to identify div_x w_m.

The complete local proof pulls back the finite interval union in step 1.1, differentiates the pulled-back integrand uniformly by the mean-value theorem and compact uniform continuity in step 1.2, uses Jacobi and change of variables in step 2.1, and applies the one-dimensional FTC to each endpoint in step 3.1. The independent Donea chapter also supports the ALE transport context.

The complete local proof pulls back the fixed-domain integral, justifies differentiation by uniform difference-quotient convergence in steps 1.1–1.2, substitutes Jacobi and changes variables in step 2.1, and applies the explicitly Countable-Choice divergence theorem in step 3.1. No discrete curved-mesh rate is inferred.
The local Definition states all period, face, positive-width Jacobian, relative-speed, and face-update conventions. No numerical theorem is imported from the thesis.
Steps 1.1–2.1 subtract the two adjacent face updates and divide by positive Delta xi. This finite identity is derived fully from the local grid Definition.

The local Algorithm specifies move, reject nonpositive new Jacobians before updating, compute the relative-speed upwind flux, and solve the conservative update. It is a definition of the selected finite scheme, not an imported result.

Step 1.1 sums periodic flux differences to zero; steps 2.1–3.1 substitute a constant state, cancel mesh-flux motion with the exact discrete GCL, and divide by positive new Jacobians. The complete proof is local.

Step 1.1 expands the update into three nonnegative coefficients under the stated CFL; step 2.1 divides by positive new cell Jacobians and uses constant preservation for row sums; step 3.1 uses mass conservation for weighted column sums and the triangle inequality. The complete proof is local.
